title: Intellectual Disability (Intellectual Developmental Disorder)
targetDescription: Deficits in intellectual and adaptive functioning with onset during the developmental period.

differentials.distinction: Involves acquired decline from a previously attained level of functioning, rather than deficits present from the developmental period.
Deficits are circumscribed to specific academic skills without global impairment of intellectual and adaptive functioning.
Impairment is limited to communication/language; nonverbal intellectual and adaptive functioning are relatively preserved.
Defined by social-communication deficits and restricted/repetitive behavior; may co-occur with intellectual disability, in which case both are diagnosed.

title: Communication Disorders
target: Communication Disorders (Language, Speech Sound, Childhood-Onset Fluency, Social Pragmatic)
targetDescription: Persistent difficulties in language, speech production, fluency, or the social use of communication.

differentials.distinction: Communication problems are part of a broader deficit in intellectual and adaptive functioning rather than a circumscribed language/speech deficit.
Includes restricted/repetitive behaviors and interests in addition to social-communication deficits; Social (Pragmatic) Communication Disorder is diagnosed only when ASD is excluded.
Communication difficulty is fully attributable to a sensory deficit and resolves/adapts with appropriate accommodation.
Language capacity is intact but the child fails to speak in specific social situations.
Language/speech is within the expected range for developmental level and cultural/linguistic context.

title: Autism Spectrum Disorder
targetDescription: Persistent deficits in social communication/interaction plus restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities, with onset in the early developmental period.

differentials.distinction: Social-communication deficits are present but restricted/repetitive behaviors are absent.
Social communication is commensurate with developmental level; diagnosed additionally when social-communication deficits exceed developmental level.
Attentional/behavioral problems without the qualitative social-communication deficits and restricted interests of ASD (may co-occur).
Early development and social communication are typically normal; failure to speak is situation-specific.
Stereotypies occur without the social-communication deficits of ASD.
Includes a period of delusions/hallucinations and follows a prodrome; ASD lacks positive psychotic symptoms.

title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
targetDescription: Persistent inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity, onset before age 12, present in ≥2 settings and impairing functioning.

differentials.distinction: Resistance to tasks reflects opposition to authority rather than an inability to sustain attention.
Inattentive appearance is limited to academically demanding tasks and stems from skill deficits.
Symptoms are commensurate with mental age; ADHD diagnosed additionally if inattention/hyperactivity exceed developmental level.
Inattention/overactivity is episodic and accompanied by mood elevation, whereas ADHD is chronic and non-episodic.
Characterized by persistent irritability and severe temper outbursts beyond the impulsivity of ADHD.
Inattention is due to worry/rumination rather than distractibility by external stimuli.
Inattention began with substance use rather than in childhood.

title: Specific Learning Disorder
targetDescription: Persistent difficulties learning and using academic skills (reading, writing, or mathematics) below expectation for age, not explained by other conditions.

differentials.distinction: Academic difficulties are part of global intellectual and adaptive impairment.

differentials.disorder: Normal academic variation / lack of instruction
differentials.distinction: Underperformance is due to inadequate instruction, absence, or environmental factors rather than a learning disorder.
Represents a decline from previously attained academic skills rather than a developmental difficulty acquiring them.
Poor academic performance stems from inattention; may co-occur with specific learning disorder.
Learning difficulty is attributable to an uncorrected sensory deficit.

title: Tic Disorders
targetDescription: Sudden, rapid, recurrent, nonrhythmic motor movements and/or vocalizations with onset before age 18.

differentials.distinction: Movements are rhythmic or sustained and not suppressible/preceded by a premonitory urge as tics are.
Abnormal movements are temporally related to a substance or medication (e.g., stimulants, neuroleptics).
Compulsions are goal-directed and preceded by an obsession, whereas complex tics are less purposeful.
Movements are rhythmic, fixed, and driven rather than the brief, variable, suppressible pattern of tics.

differentials.disorder: Movements due to another medical condition
differentials.distinction: Abnormal movements are attributable to a neurological condition (e.g., Huntington's, postviral).

title: Schizophrenia or Schizophreniform Disorder
targetDescription: Two or more active-phase symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, grossly disorganized/catatonic behavior, negative symptoms) with functional decline; ≥6 months for schizophrenia, 1–6 months for schizophreniform.

differentials.distinction: A mood episode is present for the majority of the total illness duration, with ≥2 weeks of psychosis without prominent mood symptoms.
Psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during mood episodes.
Delusions occur without the other active-phase symptoms and functioning is otherwise relatively preserved.
Duration is at least 1 day but less than 1 month with return to premorbid functioning.
Psychosis is attributable to a substance and typically remits with sustained abstinence.

differentials.disorder: Psychotic Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
differentials.distinction: Psychosis is the direct physiological consequence of a medical condition.
Prominent delusions/hallucinations are absent; social-communication deficits date from early development.
Attenuated, subthreshold psychotic-like features without frank psychosis.

title: Schizoaffective Disorder
targetDescription: An uninterrupted illness with a major mood episode concurrent with active-phase schizophrenia symptoms, plus ≥2 weeks of delusions/hallucinations without a major mood episode, with mood episodes present for the majority of the illness.

differentials.distinction: Mood episodes, if present, occupy only a minority of the total active and residual illness.

differentials.disorder: Major Depressive/Bipolar Disorder With Psychotic Features
differentials.distinction: Psychotic symptoms occur exclusively during mood episodes (no ≥2-week period of psychosis without mood symptoms).
The combined mood and psychotic picture is attributable to a substance.

differentials.disorder: Psychotic Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
differentials.distinction: Symptoms are the physiological consequence of a medical condition.

title: Delusional Disorder
targetDescription: One or more delusions for ≥1 month without other active-phase schizophrenia symptoms and with relatively preserved functioning apart from the delusion's impact.

differentials.distinction: Prominent hallucinations, disorganized speech, or negative symptoms are present in addition to delusions.
Beliefs are tied to obsessions/compulsions and were once recognized as excessive.
The fixed belief concerns a perceived appearance defect.
Delusions occur only during mood episodes.
Pervasive suspiciousness without a fixed, circumscribed delusion.
Delusions are attributable to a substance or medical condition.

title: Brief Psychotic Disorder
targetDescription: Sudden onset of ≥1 positive psychotic symptom lasting at least 1 day but less than 1 month, with eventual full return to premorbid functioning.

differentials.distinction: Symptoms persist for 1 month or longer.
Psychosis occurs in the context of a manic or major depressive episode.
Psychosis is attributable to substance intoxication/withdrawal or medication.

differentials.disorder: Psychotic Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
differentials.distinction: Psychosis is the physiological consequence of a medical condition (including delirium).
Transient stress-related paranoia/dissociation without a discrete psychotic episode.

title: Unspecified Catatonia
targetDescription: A syndrome of psychomotor disturbance (stupor, catalepsy, mutism, negativism, posturing, echophenomena, agitation) occurring in association with another disorder or medical condition.

differentials.disorder: Catatonia Associated With a Mental Disorder
differentials.distinction: Occurs during a psychotic, bipolar, or depressive disorder and is specified as such rather than 'unspecified.'

differentials.disorder: Catatonic Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
differentials.distinction: Directly caused by a medical condition.
Medication-induced hyperthermia, rigidity, and autonomic instability requiring urgent medical management.
Motor findings are explained by a defined neurological movement disorder rather than catatonia.

title: Bipolar I Disorder
targetDescription: At least one Manic Episode (≥1 week or hospitalization, with marked impairment or psychosis), usually with major depressive episodes.

differentials.distinction: Hypomanic (not full manic) episodes plus major depressive episodes; never a full manic episode.
No lifetime history of a manic or hypomanic episode.
Chronic subthreshold hypomanic and depressive symptoms that never meet full episode criteria.
≥2 weeks of psychosis occur without a mood episode.
Mood elevation is attributable to a substance/medication and does not persist beyond its physiological effect.

differentials.disorder: Bipolar Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
differentials.distinction: Mania is the direct physiological consequence of a medical condition.
Chronic, non-episodic overactivity/impulsivity without discrete mood episodes (may co-occur, especially in youth).
Mood shifts are rapid, reactive to interpersonal events, and lack sustained episodes with increased energy/decreased sleep.

title: Bipolar II Disorder
targetDescription: At least one Hypomanic Episode and at least one Major Depressive Episode, with no history of a full Manic Episode.

differentials.distinction: A full manic episode has occurred at some point.
No lifetime hypomanic episode.
Symptoms never reach full hypomanic or major depressive episode thresholds.
Affective instability is brief and reactive rather than sustained hypomanic episodes.
Hypomania is attributable to a substance and does not persist with abstinence.

title: Cyclothymic Disorder
targetDescription: ≥2 years (1 year in youth) of numerous periods of hypomanic and depressive symptoms that never meet full episode criteria, present at least half the time.

differentials.distinction: Full manic, hypomanic, or major depressive episodes have occurred.
Discrete full episodes recur frequently, unlike the chronic subthreshold fluctuation of cyclothymia.
Mood instability is reactive and tied to interpersonal stressors and identity disturbance.
Mood fluctuations are attributable to a substance or medical condition.

title: Major Depressive Disorder
targetDescription: One or more Major Depressive Episodes (≥2 weeks of depressed mood/anhedonia plus additional symptoms) without a history of mania/hypomania.

differentials.distinction: A lifetime manic or hypomanic episode has occurred.
Chronic depressed mood for ≥2 years, often at lower symptom intensity.
Depressive symptoms follow a stressor and do not meet full major depressive episode criteria.

differentials.disorder: Depressive Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
differentials.distinction: Depression is the direct physiological result of a medical condition.
Depression is attributable to a substance/medication.
Psychosis occurs for ≥2 weeks outside of mood episodes.
A normative reaction to loss that does not reflect an internal dysfunction (clinical judgment required).
Poor concentration or low mood is secondary to functional impairment without a full depressive syndrome.

title: Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia)
targetDescription: Depressed mood most of the day, more days than not, for ≥2 years (≥1 year in youth), with additional depressive symptoms and no symptom-free interval longer than 2 months.

differentials.distinction: Episodic rather than chronic; MDD and persistent depressive disorder may be diagnosed together when criteria for both are met.
History of hypomanic/manic symptoms.
Chronic low mood occurs within a primary psychotic illness.

differentials.disorder: Depressive Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition / Substance-Induced
differentials.distinction: Chronic depression is attributable to a medical condition or substance.
Enduring maladaptive traits without pervasive depressed mood (may co-occur).

title: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder
targetDescription: Mood and physical symptoms in the final premenstrual week that improve within a few days of menses onset, confirmed by prospective ratings.

differentials.distinction: An underlying disorder (e.g., MDD) is present throughout the cycle and merely worsens premenstrually.
Painful menses without the characteristic mood symptom cluster.

differentials.disorder: Major Depressive Disorder / Persistent Depressive Disorder
differentials.distinction: Mood symptoms are not confined to the luteal phase.
Symptoms are attributable to exogenous hormones.

title: Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder
targetDescription: Severe recurrent temper outbursts with persistently irritable/angry mood between outbursts, onset before age 10, diagnosed between ages 6 and 18.

differentials.distinction: Irritability is episodic with distinct periods of mood elevation/increased energy, not chronic.
DMDD requires severe outbursts and persistent inter-outburst irritability; when both sets of criteria are met, only DMDD is diagnosed.
Lacks the persistent negative mood between outbursts that characterizes DMDD.
May co-occur; distinguished by the chronic irritable mood core of DMDD.
If full criteria for DMDD and MDD are both met, DMDD is not additionally diagnosed.

title: Separation Anxiety Disorder
targetDescription: Developmentally inappropriate, excessive fear/anxiety about separation from attachment figures.

differentials.distinction: Worry spans many domains rather than focusing on separation.
Fear centers on panic symptoms or escape difficulty rather than separation from attachment figures.
Avoidance is due to fear of scrutiny, not separation.
School/social refusal relates to sensory/social intolerance rather than separation fear.
School avoidance is to pursue activities outside home rather than to stay near attachment figures.
Fear is focused on illness or trauma reminders rather than separation.

title: Selective Mutism
targetDescription: Consistent failure to speak in specific social situations where speaking is expected, despite speaking in others, interfering with functioning.

differentials.distinction: Speech difficulty is not restricted to specific social situations.
Failure to speak reflects social-communication deficits present across settings.
Broader social fear; selective mutism specifically involves not speaking and may be diagnosed alongside it.
Transient silence during adjustment to a new environment or language does not warrant the diagnosis.

title: Specific Phobia
targetDescription: Marked fear/anxiety about a specific object or situation, actively avoided, out of proportion to actual danger.

differentials.distinction: Fear spans multiple situations centered on escape/help difficulty rather than one circumscribed object.
Fear is of social scrutiny.
Avoidance relates to separation from attachment figures.
Avoidance is of trauma reminders.
Avoidance is driven by obsessions (e.g., contamination).
Panic attacks are unexpected rather than cued only by a specific phobic stimulus.

title: Social Anxiety Disorder (Social Phobia)
targetDescription: Marked fear/anxiety about social situations involving possible scrutiny, with fear of negative evaluation.

differentials.distinction: Unexpected panic attacks not limited to social situations.
Fear is of escape difficulty/incapacitation rather than scrutiny.
Worry extends to nonsocial domains and ongoing relationships.
Discomfort persists even with attachment figures present in social settings.
Social-communication deficits with lack of age-appropriate relationships; social anxiety patients retain social capacity.
Social avoidance stems from beliefs about appearance flaws.
Pervasive; frequently overlaps and both may be diagnosed.
Not markedly impairing or distressing.

title: Panic Disorder
targetDescription: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks with ≥1 month of concern about further attacks or maladaptive behavior change.

differentials.disorder: Other anxiety disorders with cued attacks
differentials.distinction: Panic attacks are expected (cued by phobic, social, or trauma stimuli) rather than unexpected.

differentials.disorder: Anxiety Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
differentials.distinction: Panic is caused by a medical condition (e.g., arrhythmia, hyperthyroidism, pheochromocytoma).
Panic attributable to a substance (e.g., caffeine, stimulants) or withdrawal.
Preoccupation with having a serious illness without recurrent unexpected panic.
May co-occur; agoraphobia is coded separately when present.

title: Agoraphobia
targetDescription: Marked fear/avoidance of ≥2 situations (public transport, open/enclosed spaces, crowds, being outside alone) due to fear that escape or help may be unavailable.

differentials.distinction: Fear involves a single situation rather than the ≥2 agoraphobic clusters.
Avoidance is due to fear of scrutiny.
Avoidance relates to separation from attachment figures.
Avoidance is of trauma reminders.
Reduced going out reflects anhedonia/amotivation rather than fear of escape difficulty.

title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
targetDescription: Excessive, hard-to-control worry about multiple domains, more days than not for ≥6 months, with somatic symptoms.

differentials.disorder: Anxiety Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition / Substance-Induced
differentials.distinction: Anxiety is attributable to a medical condition or substance.
Worry is confined to a specific focus rather than generalized.
Anxiety is driven by intrusive obsessions rather than realistic-themed worry.
Worry centers specifically on having a serious illness.
Worry is confined to a depressive episode or a stressor-related adjustment reaction.
Worry is controllable, not markedly distressing, and not accompanied by the somatic symptom burden.

title: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
targetDescription: Recurrent obsessions and/or compulsions that are time-consuming or cause significant distress/impairment.

differentials.distinction: Excessive worry about real-life concerns rather than intrusive, ego-dystonic obsessions with rituals.
Preoccupations and rituals focus specifically on perceived appearance defects.
Difficulty discarding driven by perceived need to save, not by obsessions.
Body-focused repetitive behaviors without preceding obsessions.
Preoccupation is specifically about having an illness.
Tics are not preceded by an obsession and are less purposeful.
OCD retains at least some insight in most cases; delusional disorder involves fixed non-ritualized beliefs.
Pervasive perfectionism/control as ego-syntonic traits without true obsessions/compulsions.

title: Body Dysmorphic Disorder
targetDescription: Preoccupation with perceived defects/flaws in appearance not observable or slight to others, with repetitive behaviors.

differentials.distinction: Not preoccupying, distressing, or impairing.
Concern is specifically about body weight/shape and eating behavior.
Obsessions/compulsions are not limited to appearance.
Fear of scrutiny is not based on a specific perceived appearance defect.
Appearance-related negative thoughts occur only within a depressive episode.
Preoccupation is with illness rather than appearance.

title: Hoarding Disorder
targetDescription: Persistent difficulty discarding possessions due to a perceived need to save, resulting in clutter that compromises living areas.

differentials.distinction: Accumulation results from obsessions (e.g., contamination) and is unwanted, not driven by a desire to save.
Clutter reflects psychomotor slowing/amotivation rather than saving urges.
Accumulation stems from cognitive decline.
Collecting is tied to restricted interests or delusional beliefs.
Organized, valued collections without clutter or impairment.

title: Trichotillomania (Hair-Pulling Disorder)
targetDescription: Recurrent pulling out of one's hair causing hair loss, with repeated attempts to stop.

differentials.distinction: Hair pulling is not performed in response to an obsession.
Hair removal is to correct a perceived appearance defect.
Movements are stereotyped or tic-like rather than focused hair pulling.
Pulling responds to a delusion or hallucination.
Alopecia is due to a medical condition rather than pulling.

title: Excoriation (Skin-Picking) Disorder
targetDescription: Recurrent skin picking causing lesions, with repeated attempts to stop.

differentials.distinction: Picking is not driven by an obsession.
Picking is to improve a perceived appearance defect.
Intent is to relieve negative feelings via self-harm rather than habitual picking.
Picking responds to a delusion of infestation.
Picking occurs during stimulant use (formication).
Skin lesions are due to a primary dermatologic disorder.

title: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder or Acute Stress Disorder
targetDescription: Intrusion, avoidance, negative cognition/mood alterations, and arousal following exposure to actual/threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence (>1 month = PTSD; 3 days–1 month = ASD).

differentials.distinction: Stressor is not of the required traumatic type, or the response does not meet the PTSD symptom pattern.
Intrusive thoughts are not tied to a traumatic event.
Lacks the intrusion and trauma-related avoidance symptoms.
Dissociation occurs without the full PTSD symptom picture.
Flashbacks are trauma-linked reexperiencing, not primary hallucinations/delusions.
Neurocognitive symptoms are due to the physical injury rather than the psychological trauma.

title: Adjustment Disorder
targetDescription: Clinically significant emotional/behavioral symptoms developing within 3 months of an identifiable stressor, resolving within 6 months of its termination, not meeting criteria for another disorder.

differentials.distinction: Full criteria for a specific disorder are met; adjustment disorder is a residual diagnosis.
The stressor is traumatic and the characteristic symptom pattern is present.
Symptoms are enduring traits; adjustment disorder may be diagnosed additionally if a stressor causes acute worsening.
Response is within expectable/culturally normative limits and not markedly impairing.

title: Dissociative Amnesia
targetDescription: Inability to recall important autobiographical information, usually of a traumatic/stressful nature, inconsistent with ordinary forgetting.

differentials.distinction: Memory loss is part of a broader cognitive decline with anterograde impairment.
Amnesia is for events during intoxication and attributable to the substance.
Amnesia is limited to a component of the trauma within the full PTSD picture.

differentials.disorder: Amnesia due to another medical condition (e.g., seizure, TBI)
differentials.distinction: Memory loss is the physiological consequence of a medical/neurological event.
Amnesia is feigned for external incentive or to assume the sick role.

title: Depersonalization/Derealization Disorder
targetDescription: Persistent/recurrent experiences of detachment from one's self (depersonalization) or surroundings (derealization) with intact reality testing.

differentials.distinction: Depersonalization occurs only during panic attacks or anxiety episodes.
Dissociation is part of the trauma-related symptom picture.
In psychosis, reality testing is lost; here the individual knows the experience is not real.
Symptoms are attributable to a substance (e.g., cannabis, hallucinogens) or medical condition (e.g., seizures).
Detachment occurs only within a depressive episode.

title: Somatic Symptom Disorder
targetDescription: One or more distressing somatic symptoms plus excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to them.

differentials.distinction: Somatic symptoms are minimal/absent; the focus is fear of having/acquiring illness.
A medical condition explains the symptoms and the psychological response is proportionate.
Somatic symptoms are episodic and confined to panic attacks.
Worry is generalized rather than focused on somatic symptoms.
Symptoms are specifically neurological and incompatible with recognized disease.
Somatic complaints occur only within a depressive episode.
Preoccupation is with appearance rather than somatic symptoms.

title: Illness Anxiety Disorder
targetDescription: Preoccupation with having/acquiring a serious illness, with minimal somatic symptoms and high health-related anxiety.

differentials.distinction: Prominent distressing somatic symptoms are present.
Worry spans many topics, not just illness.
Illness-related intrusive thoughts are obsessions with associated compulsions across other themes.
Health preoccupation occurs only within a depressive episode.
The illness belief is held with delusional conviction.

differentials.disorder: Adjustment reaction to real medical illness
differentials.distinction: Anxiety is a proportionate response to a genuine, serious diagnosis.

title: Conversion Disorder (Functional Neurological Symptom Disorder)
targetDescription: Altered voluntary motor or sensory function with clinical findings incompatible with recognized neurological/medical conditions.

differentials.distinction: Examination shows findings compatible with a recognized neurological disorder.
Symptoms are not specifically neurological or incompatibility is not demonstrable.
Symptoms are intentionally produced (for the sick role or external incentive).
Symptoms are dissociative (memory/identity) rather than sensorimotor.
Neurological-seeming symptoms occur only during panic attacks.

title: Psychological Factors Affecting Other Medical Conditions
target: Psychological Factors Affecting Other Medical Conditions
targetDescription: Psychological/behavioral factors that adversely affect a documented medical condition by influencing its course, treatment, or pathophysiology.

differentials.disorder: Mental disorder with a medical cause
differentials.distinction: There a psychiatric disorder is caused by the medical condition, not psychological factors worsening it.
A psychological response to the medical illness that itself meets disorder criteria, rather than factors worsening the illness.
Excessive thoughts/behaviors about symptoms dominate rather than measurable worsening of a medical condition.
Health anxiety predominates without a medical condition being worsened.

title: Factitious Disorder
targetDescription: Falsification of physical/psychological signs or symptoms, or induction of injury/disease, in the absence of obvious external rewards.

differentials.distinction: Feigning is motivated by a tangible external incentive (money, drugs, avoiding duties).
Symptoms are genuinely experienced rather than deliberately falsified.
Symptoms are not intentionally produced.
Self-harm is to relieve distress rather than to deceive and assume the sick role.
Signs are authentic and not induced or falsified.

title: Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder
targetDescription: Avoidance/restriction of food intake with nutritional/energy or psychosocial consequences, not driven by body-image concerns.

differentials.distinction: Restriction is driven by fear of weight gain and body-image disturbance.

differentials.disorder: Medical condition (e.g., GI disease, food allergy)
differentials.distinction: Restriction is fully accounted for by a medical condition.
Reduced intake is secondary to appetite loss within another disorder.
Selective eating is part of restricted/sensory features; ARFID diagnosed additionally if severe.
Does not cause nutritional deficiency, dependence on supplements, or psychosocial impairment.

title: Anorexia Nervosa
targetDescription: Restriction of intake leading to significantly low weight, intense fear of weight gain, and disturbance in experience of body weight/shape.

differentials.distinction: Body weight is maintained at or above normal despite binge-purge cycles.
Low weight without body-image disturbance or fear of weight gain.
Weight loss is due to a medical illness without the characteristic body-image disturbance.
Weight loss from appetite reduction without fear of weight gain or body-image disturbance.
Preoccupation concerns appearance features other than weight/shape.
Food refusal is due to delusions (e.g., of poisoning) rather than weight concern.

title: Bulimia Nervosa
targetDescription: Recurrent binge eating with inappropriate compensatory behaviors, ≥once weekly for 3 months, with self-evaluation unduly influenced by shape/weight.

differentials.distinction: The individual is at significantly low weight; anorexia takes precedence.
Binges occur without regular compensatory behaviors.

differentials.disorder: Major Depressive Disorder with atypical features
differentials.distinction: Overeating occurs without binge loss-of-control or compensation.
Impulsivity is not centered on binge eating.
Hyperphagia is attributable to a neurological/medical syndrome.

title: Binge-Eating Disorder
targetDescription: Recurrent binge eating with marked distress, without the regular compensatory behaviors of bulimia nervosa.

differentials.distinction: Regular inappropriate compensatory behaviors are present.
Overeating occurs without discrete binge episodes with loss of control.
Increased appetite without discrete binges with loss of control.
Overeating occurs within mood episodes.

title: Insomnia Disorder
targetDescription: Dissatisfaction with sleep quantity/quality (difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep or early awakening) ≥3 nights/week for ≥3 months with daytime impairment.

differentials.distinction: Short-lived or does not cause significant daytime impairment.
Insomnia is explained by a breathing-related, circadian rhythm, or restless legs disorder.
Attributable to a substance, medication, or caffeine.
Insomnia is fully accounted for by another disorder; insomnia disorder is added when it is an independent focus.

differentials.disorder: Sleep disturbance due to another medical condition
differentials.distinction: Caused by pain, nocturia, or other medical factors.

title: Hypersomnolence Disorder
targetDescription: Excessive sleepiness despite ≥7 hours of sleep, with prolonged sleep, difficulty being fully awake, or nonrestorative sleep, ≥3 times/week for ≥3 months.

differentials.distinction: Presence of cataplexy, sleep paralysis, hypnagogic hallucinations, and characteristic REM findings.
Sleepiness is due to sleep-disordered breathing (e.g., obstructive apnea).
Sleepiness resolves with adequate sleep opportunity.
Attributable to sedating substances or medications.
Excessive sleep occurs only within a depressive episode.

title: Sexual Dysfunctions
targetDescription: Clinically significant disturbance in sexual response or pleasure, typically ≥6 months, causing distress.

differentials.distinction: Dysfunction is attributable to a substance or medication (e.g., SSRIs, antihypertensives).

differentials.disorder: Sexual dysfunction due to another medical condition
differentials.distinction: Fully explained by a medical condition (vascular, neurologic, endocrine).
Dysfunction is better explained by another disorder (e.g., major depressive disorder).

differentials.disorder: Severe relationship distress or other stressors
differentials.distinction: Dysfunction is attributable to relationship problems, partner factors, or contextual stressors.
Response is within normal limits given age, stimulation, and context, and is not distressing.

title: Gender Dysphoria
targetDescription: Marked incongruence between one's experienced/expressed gender and assigned gender, with clinically significant distress or impairment.

differentials.distinction: Gender-atypical behavior without the marked incongruence and distress required for the diagnosis.
Preoccupation is with a perceived appearance defect rather than gender incongruence.
Cross-dressing is for sexual arousal without a desire to be the other gender.
Any belief about being another gender is delusional rather than an identity experience.

title: Oppositional Defiant Disorder
targetDescription: A pattern of angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behavior, or vindictiveness lasting ≥6 months.

differentials.distinction: Involves violation of others' basic rights and major societal norms, beyond defiance.
Severe temper outbursts plus persistent irritability; when both are met, DMDD is diagnosed instead.
Noncompliance stems from inattention/impulsivity rather than deliberate defiance (often co-occurs).
Oppositional behavior occurs only during mood episodes.
Characterized by serious aggressive outbursts rather than a broad defiant pattern.
Behavior is within expectable frequency/intensity for developmental stage.

title: Intermittent Explosive Disorder
targetDescription: Recurrent impulsive/anger-based aggressive outbursts grossly out of proportion to provocation, not premeditated.

differentials.distinction: Aggression is instrumental/premeditated and part of a broader antisocial pattern.
Persistent irritable mood between outbursts; DMDD takes precedence in youth when both are met.
Outbursts occur during manic episodes.
Aggression occurs in the context of substance use.
Aggression is part of a pervasive personality pattern.

differentials.disorder: Aggression due to another medical condition
differentials.distinction: Outbursts are the physiological consequence of a medical condition (e.g., head trauma).

title: Conduct Disorder
targetDescription: A repetitive, persistent pattern of behavior violating others' basic rights or major age-appropriate societal norms.

differentials.distinction: Defiance and irritability without violation of others' basic rights.
The adult (≥18) continuation; conduct disorder is required before age 15.
Impulsive rule-breaking without a sustained pattern of rights violations (often co-occurs).
Antisocial behavior occurs only during mood episodes.
Aggression is impulsive outbursts without the broader pattern of nonaggressive conduct violations.
Conduct disturbance is a time-limited reaction to a stressor.

title: Substance Use Disorders
targetDescription: A problematic pattern of substance use leading to clinically significant impairment/distress, with impaired control, social impairment, risky use, and pharmacological criteria.

differentials.distinction: Use without impaired control, compulsion, or the required impairment criteria.
Refers to the psychiatric syndromes caused by the substance rather than the use pattern itself.
A non-substance (behavioral) addiction sharing features but not involving substance ingestion.

differentials.disorder: Primary mental disorder with secondary use
differentials.distinction: Use is self-medication of a primary disorder present during abstinent periods.

title: Gambling Disorder
targetDescription: Persistent, recurrent problematic gambling leading to clinically significant impairment or distress.

differentials.distinction: Gambling is disciplined, limited, and not associated with loss of control or impairment.
Excessive gambling occurs only during mood elevation.
Gambling is part of a broader antisocial pattern (may co-occur).
Shares addictive features but involves substance ingestion.

title: Delirium
targetDescription: An acute, fluctuating disturbance of attention and awareness with an additional cognitive disturbance, developing over hours to days from a medical cause, substance, or multiple etiologies.

differentials.distinction: Chronic, stable cognitive decline with preserved attention/awareness (though delirium can be superimposed).
Consciousness/attention are intact and onset is not acute-fluctuating.
No global attentional disturbance with a medical/substance cause.
Attention/awareness are not acutely and globally impaired with fluctuation.

title: Major or Mild Neurocognitive Disorder
targetDescription: Acquired decline from a previous level in ≥1 cognitive domain; major NCD interferes with independence, mild NCD does not.

differentials.distinction: Acute, fluctuating attentional disturbance rather than a stable decline.
Deficits are developmental and lifelong, not an acquired decline.
Cognitive complaints improve with treatment of the depressive episode.
Age-expected cognitive change without significant decline or impairment.
Decline is attributable to a substance/medication.
Cognitive impairment occurs within a primary psychotic illness.

title: Paranoid Personality Disorder
targetDescription: Pervasive distrust and suspiciousness such that others' motives are interpreted as malevolent, beginning by early adulthood.

differentials.distinction: Involves fixed delusions rather than pervasive but non-delusional suspiciousness.
Includes frank psychotic symptoms.
Adds cognitive-perceptual distortions and eccentricity.
Detachment without prominent suspiciousness.

differentials.disorder: Personality change due to another medical condition / substance-related
differentials.distinction: Suspiciousness is attributable to a medical condition or substance.

title: Schizoid Personality Disorder
targetDescription: Pervasive detachment from social relationships and a restricted range of emotional expression.

differentials.distinction: Adds cognitive-perceptual distortions and eccentric behavior.
Social withdrawal stems from fear of rejection, with a desire for closeness.
Includes restricted/repetitive behaviors and early developmental social-communication deficits.
History of active-phase psychotic symptoms.
Social withdrawal is episodic and mood-linked.

title: Schizotypal Personality Disorder
targetDescription: Pervasive social/interpersonal deficits with acute discomfort in close relationships, plus cognitive-perceptual distortions and eccentric behavior.

differentials.distinction: Involves frank, sustained psychotic symptoms rather than attenuated ones.
Lack the cognitive-perceptual distortions and eccentricity of schizotypal.
Social deficits stem from early developmental communication impairment and restricted interests.
Attenuated psychotic-like features are attributable to a substance or medical condition.

title: Antisocial Personality Disorder
targetDescription: A pervasive pattern of disregard for and violation of others' rights since age 15, in an individual ≥18 with evidence of conduct disorder before age 15.

differentials.distinction: The youth (<18) precursor; antisocial personality disorder requires age ≥18.
Antisocial acts occur only in service of substance use, without a lifelong pattern (may co-occur).
Exploitation without the impulsivity, aggression, and deceit for personal gain seen in antisocial.
Irresponsible/antisocial behavior occurs only during mood elevation.
Illegal acts occur without the pervasive personality pattern.

title: Borderline Personality Disorder
targetDescription: A pervasive pattern of instability in interpersonal relationships, self-image, and affect, with marked impulsivity.

differentials.distinction: Mood shifts are sustained episodes with increased energy/decreased sleep, versus brief reactive shifts.
Chronic emptiness/instability is a personality trait rather than a discrete episode.
Attention-seeking without the self-destructiveness, emptiness, and rage of borderline.
Self-image is grandiose and stable rather than unstable.
Instability is tied to trauma reexperiencing rather than a pervasive personality pattern.
Impulsivity/instability occur only during substance use.

title: Histrionic Personality Disorder
targetDescription: A pervasive pattern of excessive emotionality and attention seeking.

differentials.distinction: Adds self-destructiveness, chronic emptiness, and identity disturbance.
Attention seeking is to affirm superiority rather than for nurturance.
Reliance on others without the dramatic, seductive attention seeking.
Focus is on physical symptoms rather than dramatic interpersonal style.

title: Narcissistic Personality Disorder
targetDescription: A pervasive pattern of grandiosity, need for admiration, and lack of empathy.

differentials.distinction: Exploitation is accompanied by impulsivity, aggression, and deceit for material gain.
Attention seeking is for nurturance rather than to confirm superiority.
Self-image is unstable rather than grandiose.
Grandiosity is episodic and accompanied by mood/energy change.
Preoccupation with order/perfectionism rather than admiration and grandiosity.

title: Avoidant Personality Disorder
targetDescription: A pervasive pattern of social inhibition, feelings of inadequacy, and hypersensitivity to negative evaluation.

differentials.distinction: Largely overlapping; both may be diagnosed. Personality disorder is broader and earlier-onset.
Detachment reflects lack of desire for relationships, not fear of rejection.
Focus is on being cared for rather than on avoiding humiliation.
Avoidance is of situations where escape is difficult rather than of social scrutiny.

title: Dependent Personality Disorder
targetDescription: A pervasive and excessive need to be taken care of, leading to submissive/clinging behavior and fears of separation.

differentials.distinction: Reacts to abandonment with rage/emptiness rather than submission and seeking a new caretaker.
Uses gregarious, demanding attention seeking rather than submissive dependence.
Withdraws from relationships until certain of acceptance, rather than clinging.

differentials.disorder: Dependence due to a medical condition / mood disorder
differentials.distinction: Dependent behavior is secondary to another disorder.

title: Obsessive-Compulsive Personality Disorder
targetDescription: A pervasive preoccupation with orderliness, perfectionism, and mental/interpersonal control at the expense of flexibility and efficiency.

differentials.distinction: Presence of true obsessions and compulsions, whereas OCPD involves ego-syntonic traits without them.
Clinically significant hoarding may warrant a separate diagnosis.
Perfectionism serves self-image of superiority rather than orderliness/control for its own sake.

differentials.disorder: Personality change due to another medical condition
differentials.distinction: Traits are an acquired change attributable to a medical condition.

title: Personality Change Due to Another Medical Condition
target: Personality Change Due to Another Medical Condition
targetDescription: A persistent personality disturbance representing a change from the individual's previous characteristic pattern, caused by the physiological effects of a medical condition.

differentials.distinction: Lifelong pattern rather than an acquired change from a medical cause.
Personality change occurs within a broader disturbance of consciousness or cognition.
Change is attributable to a substance/medication rather than a medical condition.

differentials.disorder: Other mental disorders due to a medical condition
differentials.distinction: Presentation is dominated by mood, psychosis, or anxiety rather than personality change.

title: Paraphilic Disorders
targetDescription: Recurrent, intense atypical sexual interests causing distress/impairment or entailing harm/risk to others (or nonconsenting persons).

differentials.distinction: The interest does not cause distress/impairment or harm to others, so no disorder is diagnosed.
Hypersexual or atypical behavior occurs only during mood elevation or intoxication.
Disinhibited sexual behavior results from cognitive decline.
Sexual intrusive thoughts are ego-dystonic obsessions, not paraphilic arousal.
Sexual offenses occur within a broader antisocial pattern rather than a specific paraphilic interest.
